experiment: IO-bound cross-layer query-free prefetch (gate for the systems-module pivot)
setup: SEER sim, Llama-3.1-8B, mooncake 4096, budget 0.10, io_mode=analytical ell_bar=6000us (simulated CPU/NVMe offload), h2o policy
verdict: GATE PASSED in principle: cross-layer prefetch (prev-layer attention top-K) hides 68% of recall IO and cuts TPOT 23% in the IO-bound regime.
honest_scope: Source = oracle_prev (prev-layer ATTENTION top-K). Realizable QUERY-FREE only where you HAVE prev-layer attention over the candidate blocks: the FlexGen-style full-attention OFFLOAD regime (all KV offloaded but attended) -> predict layer-l hot blocks from layer-(l-1) attention (87.5% recall, a layer ahead), fetch ONLY those instead of ALL. FlexGen fetches all KV/layer; vLLM keeps KV in GPU. Neither does attention-predicted selective cross-layer prefetch. THIS is the novel module.

In the EVICTION-recall regime (demoted blocks masked) query-free prefetch is INERT (can't see demoted blocks' attention) -- there the realizable signal needs the query (InfiniGen q.k), confirming the earlier inert finding. So the module's home is FlexGen-style offload, not eviction-recall.

IO here is SIMULATED (analytical ell_bar). A real contribution needs measured offload (CPU/NVMe) + the realizable prev-layer-attention source, and it is a SYSTEMS contribution (MLSys-ish), not the ICDM data-mining core.
bottom_line: First real positive of the design search: a novel, grounded systems module (selective attention-predicted cross-layer prefetch for offloaded serving) with a demonstrated 23% TPOT cut at the cross-layer-persistence ceiling. Worth a scoped systems build; honest about the realizable-source + real-offload gaps.
